properties.project_name: P2 -- open-space strip between Mission Creek and Channel St
properties.digitized_from: Real-gap-fragment technique: bbox.difference(street buffer, src/street_geometry.py)..difference(all already-tracked parcels/approx polygons) over the creek corridor between Mission Creek and Channel St yielded a numbered set of disconnected real scraps of unclaimed land; the owner, viewing the numbered map against Esri satellite imagery, picked fragment 7 (the paved/planted strip along the creek's near bank) and fragment 9 (a paved path further southeast, separated from 7 by a landscaping/tree strip not itself captured as its own fragment) and specified how to combine them.
properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-20 via the numbered real-gap-fragment technique established for P8 (see that record): generated a map of every disconnected real (street-buffer- and already-tracked-polygon-excluded) scrap of land in the creek/Channel St corridor between about where P8 hands off (near the roundabout) and the creek bend northeast of it. Two rounds of owner review (first pass, then a request to extend the view further northeast) converged on: fragment 7, truncated at its north edge along the same real line P8's fragment 4 was cut on (a line fit through the north corners of P8's fragments 34/41/17, confirmed colinear to ~5e-8 deg) -- at fragment 7's own longitude range this line lands almost exactly on its existing north boundary (matching to within ~0.00015 deg at the fragment's far corner), separating the real open water of Mission Creek (the ~9,854 sqm piece north of the line, discarded) from the real paved/planted strip along the near bank (~4,855 sqm, kept). The owner then specified translating fragment 9 (a separate paved path, ~7,932 sqm) north to merge with the truncated fragment 7, closing a real but narrow (~17-22m) planting-strip gap between the two rather than tracing that gap directly -- picked a 0.0002 deg (~22m) north shift, comfortably past the ~0.000156 deg (~17.3m) minimum needed for the two shapes to touch, for a clean overlapping seam rather than a knife-edge join. Final shape is the union of truncated-7 and shifted-9 (~12,224 sqm). PRE-CLIPPED 2026-09-20 against the real street buffer (src/street_geometry.py) before committing: the union (fragment 7 truncated + fragment 9 translated north) reached into a real paved area near the boat-dock access road at its northeast end -- join_approximate.py --strict flagged this as a 25% MAJOR CLIP, at the threshold where the checker asks for a direct look rather than trusting the auto-clip. Inspected directly against Esri satellite imagery: the removed area is a real paved road/driveway crossing plus the road-side verge, not a mispositioned trace, so committed the pre-clipped result (12,224 sqm -> 9,128 sqm) directly rather than relying on the pipeline's silent auto-clip every run. Splits into three pieces: the near-bank strip (4,977 sqm), the road-side strip that was fragment 9 (3,896 sqm), and a small separate grassy patch near the boat dock (255 sqm) that the clip revealed as disconnected from the other two. TRIMMED 2026-09-20: dropped the small (~255 sqm) disconnected triangle near the boat dock at P2's northeast end per the owner's review -- an artifact of the street clip, not real intended P2 open space. Final: 2 pieces, ~8,873 sqm. TRIMMED AGAIN 2026-09-20: the kept near-bank strip still had a thin (1-9m wide) spike continuing northeast past a natural waist (width narrows to ~1.1m at lat 37.7728) up to the edge of the analysis bbox -- the same 'weird thin edge' pattern flagged and removed elsewhere in this session (P8's fragment-4 spike, fragment 18's ribbon). Cut at that waist and dropped the spike (~619 sqm) per the owner's review. Final: 2 pieces, ~8,254 sqm. REVERTED THE STREET-CLIP 2026-09-20: the owner reviewed the clipped 2-piece result and pointed out it broke the continuity the fragment-9 translation was specifically meant to achieve -- the clip was correctly removing a real paved road, but that road runs almost the full length between the near-bank strip and the road-side strip, so clipping split one corridor into two disconnected pieces. Chosen fix (owner's pick among 3 options offered): set street_clip_exempt=true, the same opt-out already used for Pier 70's 20th Street Plaza -- this record represents the park-corridor CONCEPT, which crosses the road at grade, not today's paved-road extent. Reverted to the pre-clip, spike-trimmed continuous shape (single Polygon, ~11,652 sqm; the same waist-cut technique removed the same northeast spike directly from this unclipped version, at a very similar cut latitude -- 37.7730 instead of 37.7728). STATUS UPDATED 2026-09-20: owner confirmed P2 is under construction (planned -> under_construction), while P7/P9 remain planned and P10 remains complete.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE, AND KNOWINGLY DISPLACED -- fragment 9's real digitized position is ~17-22m south of where it's drawn here; the owner directed this shift to close a real gap (a planting/tree strip between two paved features) with a single deliberate translation rather than tracing that gap's own real edges. Fragment 7's kept portion is a real computed shape (street/creek/already-tracked-polygon-bounded), not hand-traced. Overlaps the already-tracked real 'Mission Creek Park' polygon (which the owner has directed be unioned to include this record and P8, per their own framing that Mission Creek Park will evolve to encompass P1+P2+P8) and may overlap the real Mission Creek Park -- east reach (Pavilion to 4th St bridge) record (P1) at its northeast end, near the edge of the analysis window used to generate the candidate fragments -- not reconciled with either. STREET-CLIP EXEMPT: this record deliberately claims area that includes today's real paved road crossing the corridor (a park-corridor concept, not today's satellite extent) -- same class of exception as Pier 70's 20th Street Plaza. Do not treat this as a mispositioned trace; it's an intentional choice to keep the corridor continuous rather than split by a road the park is meant to cross at grade.
properties.notes: OCII plan parcel P2. Runs along the near (south/west) bank of Mission Creek between the creek and Channel St, from about where P8 hands off near the Mission Bay Circle roundabout, northeast toward the creek bend.
